reference_matrix: central-difference Jacobian of the nonlinear reduced field F(x_d, u) = [x_d'; v_RDC] with inner re-solve of the algebraic block at every evaluation (DEC-051 model with PSS); h_states=1e-6, h_refs=1e-5

CAUSE_OF_THE_1.7_PERCENT_DISCREPANCY.finding: produced by the DEC-051 harness, not by the E9 analytic assembly: e9h_predictor.build() evaluates the original RDC law at u0 = [st['pset'], st['qset']], and run_dec051_h4.load_eq() rebuilt st from the pre-event state (pset = pn, qset = qn) without writing the equilibrium references into it. The capability factors g_P, g_Q (and the RDC derivatives) were evaluated at the wrong references (largest error in Qset 0.249 pu); the slowest mode depends on g_Q of SG31, which explains 504 s vs 427 s.
CAUSE_OF_THE_1.7_PERCENT_DISCREPANCY.fix: assign st['pset'], st['qset'] = u* before build(); analytic and numerical Jacobians then agree at the finite-difference accuracy
CAUSE_OF_THE_1.7_PERCENT_DISCREPANCY.consequence_for_history: E13 and DEC-050 call build() inside a live B2 replay where st['pset'], st['qset'] are the live references (run_b3_ieee39 updates them every step): no evidence of an analytic-assembly error there. What remains true for E9-A/E13/DEC-050 is the omission of the PSS states. The DEC-051 statement 'the analytic assembly of E9-A/E9-H/DEC-050 has entry errors up to 1.7 %' is WITHDRAWN (INVALIDATED); the numerical Jacobian used by DEC-051 was correct.

coordinates: quotient coordinates e = Qm xi; scaled e_s = D e, D = diag(1/max(|xi*|, 0.1)) (DEC-051)

delta_A_bound.blocked_operation: A validated ||E||_2 needs (i) interval enclosures of the first and second derivatives of the 706 ANDES equations (250 states + 456 algebraic variables; compiled numpy callables without interval or AD backend; pyinterval, jax and autograd are not installed), (ii) an enclosure of the implicit elimination of the 486 x 486 algebraic block and of its derivative, (iii) interval evaluation of the RDC law (capability factors with positive parts, graph Laplacian) and of the discrete limiter logic, (iv) a validated bound of the finite-difference truncation error (third derivatives) and of the location error of the exact equilibrium. None is available; step studies are consistency checks only.
